**Blocker — `podterm.py` can return a truncated exit status when the marker is fragmented.**

Both terminal-marker regexes use `$`, which also matches at the end of the accumulated buffer. If a websocket chunk ends after the `4` in `END<tag> 42`, the detection loop treats `END<tag> 4` as complete, breaks before receiving `2\n`, and the final parser exits **4 instead of 42**. The duplicate-marker and range checks do not prevent this.

The fake transport’s fixed midpoint split does not force this case, and the live one-digit 0/7 probes cannot expose it.

Require the complete marker line—including its line terminator, e.g. `\r?\n` as appropriate—before breaking or parsing, preferably using one shared full-line regex. Add a regression that splits a multi-digit status between digits and asserts the original status. Do not commit as-is.
